title: Preprimary education laws and women’s gender attitudes, empowerment and reproductive autonomy in 117 low- and middle-income countries
title_zh: 低收入和中等收入国家117个国家中学前教育法律与妇女性别态度、赋权与生殖自主权
abstract: Preprimary education is central to the global education agenda, including Sustainable Development Goal 4.2. Despite global momentum in low- and middle-income countries, cross-national evidence on long-term outcomes associated with preprimary education legislation remains limited. Here we applied a matrix-completion approach with subgroup and sensitivity analyses using 495 nationally representative surveys from 1990 to 2024, covering nearly 6.7 million women across 117 countries. Eligibility under the legislation was associated with higher educational enrolment and completion, and with more gender-egalitarian attitudes, more favourable empowerment-related behaviours and greater reproductive autonomy. For example, eligibility was associated with higher female primary-school enrolment (1.21 percentage points (pp); 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.52 to 1.91; P < 0.001) and completion (0.75 pp; 95% CI 0.24 to 1.25; P = 0.004), greater disapproval of wife-beating (1.04 pp; 95% CI 0.53 to 1.56; P < 0.001), greater participation in decisions about husbands’ earnings (3.25 pp; 95% CI 2.50 to 4.00; P < 0.001) and greater ever use of contraception (2.96 pp; 95% CI 2.33 to 3.59; P < 0.001). Eligibility under the legislation was also associated with lower rates of adolescent childbearing (−2.41 pp; 95% CI −2.67 to −2.14; P < 0.001) and child marriage (−0.43 pp; 95% CI −0.71 to −0.15; P = 0.003). These findings provide cross-national evidence directly relevant to ongoing policy discussions surrounding Sustainable Development Goal 4.2 and broader global development agendas, while emphasizing the importance of implementation capacity and equitable system expansion. Lou et al. find that eligibility for preprimary education is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes, greater empowerment and reproductive autonomy, and lower levels of adolescent marriage and childbearing across low- and middle-income countries.
abstract_zh: 学前教育是全球教育议题的核心，包括可持续发展目标4.2。尽管低收入和中等收入国家普遍进展，但关于学前教育立法与长期结果的跨国证据仍然有限。本研究利用矩阵填充方法，结合分组和敏感性分析，利用1990至2024年间1990至2024年间的495项全国代表性调查，涵盖近670万名来自117个国家的女性。在立法范围内的资格与更高的教育入学和完成率、更具性别平等的态度、更有利的赋权相关行为以及更大的生殖自主权相关。例如，资格与更高的女童小学入学率（1.21个百分点（pp）；95%置信区间（CI）0.52至1.91；P<0.001）和完成率（0.75 pp；95% CI 0.24至1.25；P=0.004）以及对妻子被打的更强反对态度（1.04 pp；95% CI 0.53至1.56；P<0.001）、对丈夫收入决策的更大参与（3.25 pp；95% CI 2.50至4.00；P<0.001）以及更广泛的避孕药使用（2.96 pp；95% CI 2.33至3.59；P<0.001）相关。立法资格还与青少年生育率降低（−2.41 pp；95% CI −2.67至−2.14；P<0.001）以及童婚率降低（−0.43 pp；95% CI −0.71至−0.15；P=0.003）相关。这些发现直接关系到可持续发展目标4.2以及更广泛的全球发展议题的政策讨论，同时强调了实施能力和公平系统扩展的重要性。Lou等人发现，学前教育资格与低收入和中等收入国家性别平等态度、更大的赋权与生殖自主权以及较低的青少年婚姻和生育水平相关。
